newsitem.title: JAPAN: Six top DKB executives resign amid scandal.
newsitem.headline: Six top DKB executives resign amid scandal.

text.p: Scandal-tainted Dai-Ichi Kangyo Bank Ltd (DKB) announced on Monday that six of its executives, including chairman Tadashi Okuda and vice president Ichiro Fujita, had resigned from the company.
The six, who all resigned last Friday, also included senior managing director Takeo Fukushima and former chairman Kuniji Miyazaki, the bank said in a statement.
Fujita and Fukushima were arrested on Friday on suspicion of making illegal loans to a racketeer at the centre of a payoff scandal which also involves Nomura Securities Co Ltd.
The bank announced a sweeping management shake-up last week, saying that Fujita and 20 senior executives would resign after its annual shareholders' meeting on June 27.
However, the arrests of Fujita and Fukushima speeded up the resignation plans, a bank spokeswoman said.
The spokeswoman said the bank asked Okuda to resign as he had admitted that he knew about the existence of non-performing loans to a racketeer-linked company in January 1995.
Miyazaki and another adviser, Tetsuo Fujimori, resigned to take responsibility for their relationship with a former publishing company president who had introduced the racketeer to DKB, she said.
The sixth executive did not resign because of the scandal, she said.
